7.13.m: Vyāsa said: / In the month of Jyeṣṭha, O foremost twice-born, one should worship the Blessed Janārdana / with a devotional disposition, bathing him with cool waters.
Anointment should be given, as well as fragrant myrobalan / and sweet-scented oil, day after day to Hari in the summer season.
In a well-perfumed and cool temple that is exceedingly delightful, / one should place the Beloved of Kamalā each day in an assembly pavilion.
One should not place the husband of Kamalā in a place exposed to the sun, O leader of the twice-born, / nor in a woodshed with smoke, nor in a lying-in room.
Fanned with white, very long chowries, / well-pleased in the month of Jyeṣṭha, what will the husband of Kamalā not grant, O best of the twice-born?
Hari, fanned in the heat with fans made of peacock feathers, / grants everything desired in no time at all, O virtuous one.
Those by whom Viṣṇu is fanned in summer with the breeze of a palm fan / or with the breeze of pure cloth—all of them go to heaven.
One who applies fragrant pastes to his limbs, / and to Hari in the summer with sandalwoods, enters the body of Mādhava.
At the onset of heat, O foremost twice-born, he is liberated [from suffering]; there is no doubt of this. / In a garden of blossoming flowers, as well as in a forest of tulasī,
one should place Viṣṇu at twilight in a place with a gentle breeze. / By whoever Viṣṇu is adorned with garlands of trumpet flowers
in the month of Jyeṣṭha, he is to be recognized as one who has performed a thousand horse sacrifices. / But the person who offers a pearl necklace in summer to the Lord of Śrī,
to him Hari grants kingship in birth after birth. / Whoever adorns Śrī Kṛṣṇa with a garland of jewels in the summer,
hear from me, O twice-born, as I declare the fruit of his merit: / As long as Brahmā creates this entire universe, O Jaimini,
so long will he abide in the world of Viṣṇu, adorned with a garland of gems. / And whoever [adorns him] with gold ornaments and with silver ornaments,
adorns Kṛṣṇa in the summer, he too attains that fruit. / But whoever offers a colourful couch with a pillow
to Hari, the God of gods, is never sorrowful. / Heavy garments should not be given in the summer time
to Hari, O best of brāhmaṇas; pure, fine cloth should be given. / Whoever worships Hari with divine, fragrant, imperishable fruits,
having gone to Śakra's city at the end, gladly drinks nectar. / Whoever worships the Lord of Kamalā with divine priyāla fruits,
he too attains that fruit; what need of many words? / Whoever, in the summer heat, [gives] very cool barley gruel to Hari,
combined with various condiments, [if he is] a Vaiṣṇava devoted in faith— / in the month of Āṣāḍha, O best of brāhmaṇas, to the God of gods, the teacher of the world,
having bathed him with curd and worshiped him with devotion, that wise man / never again drinks milk from a mother's breast.
At the onset of clouds, he who worships Hari, who is dark as a raincloud, with kadamba flowers, / O Brahmin sage, attains the supreme path.
Whoever [decorates] the pavilion resembling blazing fire with garlands of kadamba flowers, / O best of Brahmins, obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice.
Worshiped with fragrant ketakī flowers, the husband of Kamalā / takes away every sorrow of men, O best of the twice-born.
Worshiped with the divine, well-ripened fruits of the jackfruit tree mixed with clarified butter, / the Lord Viṣṇu grants the highest sovereignty.
A Vaiṣṇava wishing for liberation, O best of the twice-born, / should offer curd and cooked rice to Hari every day with faith in the month of Āṣāḍha.
Whichever Vaiṣṇava person gives fresh butter to Kṛṣṇa, / cleansed of all sins, goes to the world of Brahmā.
Whoever worships the Supreme Self with śephālikā flowers / and with yūthikā blossoms goes to the supreme abode.
whoever worships Hari with blooming, fragrant jasmine flowers, / by the merit of that, O twice-born one, he will have such merit as cannot [be measured].
Worshipping Janārdana, the friend of the world, with tuber-blossoms and bakula flowers, / a human being attains every desire in this world.
Whoever worships Hari with grand blossoms / and with blooming kurubakas—with him Hari is always pleased.
Whoever worships Viṣṇu with sairīyaka flowers, / and whoever worships with prasū blossoms and oleander blossoms, goes to Hari's presence.
And whoever offers parched grains mixed with clarified butter to Hari in Śrāvaṇa, / in his house, O Brahmin sage, prosperity faces in every direction.
In the month of Bhādra, O best of the twice-born, a wise man should worship with faith / the spotless Nārāyaṇa, the bestower of the four aims of life.
In a newly constructed house, free from all troubles, / one should place the lotus-eyed Lord Janārdana.
A man should certainly not place Hari in an old room / that is infested with gnats, mosquitoes, and flies.
Nor in a house that is muddy, with a falling doorway, or leaking walls, / should the wise man place Hari, the Supreme Lord, during the rains.
Whatever man makes a variegated canopy in the temple of Viṣṇu, / O best of the twice-born, goes to the world of the Moon.
At night, with various kinds of incense in the temple of the Lord of the earth, / one should ward off stinging flies and mosquitoes at the time of worship.
Having covered Acyuta lying on his couch with mosquito nets, / one should place Viṣṇu in a divine temple at night during the rainy season.
Likewise with fragrant, fresh kahlāra petals, / a mortal seeking liberation should worship the lord of gods day by day in the month of Bhādra.
Janārdana is not to be worshiped with ketakī flowers in Bhādra, / because in the month of Bhādrapada the ketakī becomes like liquor.
Whoever worships the delight of the Yadus with ripe, divine palmyra fruits, / never again experiences the great misery of dwelling in a womb.
Whatever mortal offers ripe palmyra fruit with clarified butter and milk to the enemy of Mura / with faith, goes to the temple of Hari.
In the month of Bhādra, O best of the twice-born, a Vaiṣṇava should offer palmyra cake / with clarified butter to Hari for the sake of attaining solitude [with the divine].
In the month of Bhādrapada, O Brahmin, a Vaiṣṇava person who is a seeker of liberation / must not eat leafy vegetables, nor eat at night.
In the month of Āśvina, O best of brāhmaṇas, [to worship] Keśava, the destroyer of distress: / the water which is offered by men to Hari in the morning,
the Lord of Kamalā receives that water like nectar. / And what water is offered at midday to the Disc-wielder,
it is to be known as mere water; he receives it as such, O best of the twice-born. / But the water which is offered in the afternoon to Govinda,
that water becomes equal to blood; therefore Hari does not accept it. / Therefore, O best of the twice-born, one should worship Hari in the morning;
he obtains every desire through the compassion of Keśava. / Wearing only a single cloth, O best of brāhmaṇas, one should not perform worship of Hari;
or even if he performs worship in that way, Keśava does not accept it. / And whoever performs worship of Hari with an unwashed cloth,
that worship becomes fruitless, and Viṣṇu is not pleased. / But by those people by whom worship of the Disc-wielder is performed with untied hair,
they do not attain the fruit of worship, and that [worship] is taken by Bali. / If worship of the Lord of the world is performed in an unconsecrated room,
that worship, O best of brāhmaṇas, is indeed seized by Bali. / Bathing, deity-worship, giving, and worship of the ancestors—
a wise man does not perform these without a tilaka mark, O brāhmaṇa. / Whatever meritorious rite is performed without having applied tilaka marks,
all that turns to ash, and the agent becomes an inhabitant of hell. / On whose body are seen marks with the conch, disc, mace, and lotus,
he is to be known as Acyuta himself, O best of brāhmaṇas! / The Vaiṣṇava who marks the conch and lotus on his right arm,
and the disc and mace on the left, he is Viṣṇu—there is no doubt about this. / Whoever draws a lotus on the right arm above the conch,
all his evil is destroyed in an instant. / And whoever, O twice-born one, draws the mace above the disc on the left arm,
the immortal gods, headed by Śakra, bow down to him, O best of the twice-born. / And the wise person who draws the pair of Murāri's feet upon his forehead,
even a sinner, upon seeing him, is freed from evil. / Whoever draws the eight-syllabled great mantra, the Fish, and the Tortoise upon his chest,
that best of Vaiṣṇavas purifies the three worlds. / One whose body is marked daily with the weapons of Kṛṣṇa,
to him Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of the world, grants the supreme abode. / Whatever action a man performs whose body is marked with Kṛṣṇa's weapons,
whether auspicious or inauspicious, all of it becomes inexhaustible. / Dānavas, Rākṣasas, ghosts, and vetālas,
piśācas, serpents, yakṣas, and vidyādharas, / kinnaras, guhyakas, planetary spirits, and children's demon-seizers,
kūṣmāṇḍas, ḍākinīs, and other obstacle-makers— / all flee in fear upon seeing one marked with Kṛṣṇa's weapons.
Elephants, leopards, and other forest dwellers / flee in fear as soon as they see one marked with Kṛṣṇa's weapons.
Jaundice and other major diseases that strike down the body from bodily form— / whatever person beholds with devotion one whose body is marked with Kṛṣṇa's weapons,
that man attains the fruit equal to the sight of Kṛṣṇa. / Whoever worships Hari in the month of Āśvina with tripartite dūrvā grass,
his lineage continues uninterrupted like dūrvā grass. / Whoever offers a cucumber to Hari in the month of Āśvina,
grief is never born in his heart, O twice-born one. / And when Kārtika arrives, the auspicious best among all months,
a wise person should worship Dāmodara, the God of gods, with devotion. / In the month of Kārtika, O best of brāhmaṇas, for the purpose of pleasing Viṣṇu,
the wise person should perform the morning bath according to the prescribed rule. / Whoever gives up meat and sexual intercourse in the month of Kārtika,
freed from sins acquired in other births, goes to the supreme state. / When the sun enters the sign of Tulā, the morning bath, O best of the twice-born,
sacrificial food, and celibacy destroy great sins. / [Whoever] indulges in meat and sexual intercourse in the month of Kārtika,
birth after birth, O best of brāhmaṇas, he becomes a village pig. / Eating twice, another's food, and oil: a Vaiṣṇava
should strictly avoid these when the month of Kārtika arrives. / But whoever offers a lamp in the sky for Dāmodara,
I shall declare his fruit in brief; listen, O twice-born one: / freed from sins such as brāhmaṇa-slaughter, which bestow suffering,
having gone to Dāmodara's realm, he stays for the duration of a crore of yugas. / Beholding the lamp burning in the sky, the thirty [gods] headed by Vāsava,
all delighted, say thus to one another: / “This one is the best among the meritorious, intent on the worship of Keśava,
who offers a lamp to the Disc-wielder in the month of Kārtika.” / In the month of Kārtika, O best of brāhmaṇas, Hari is always pleased with him.
Whoever gives an inexhaustible lamp in Hari's temple in Kārtika, / day after day that person attains the fruit of a horse sacrifice.
Whoever worships Hari with a hundred thousand tulasī leaves in Kārtika / attains the fruit of a hundred thousand horse sacrifices.
Whoever worships imperishable Viṣṇu with a hundred thousand bilva leaves / attains supreme liberation through the grace of the Lord of the world.
Whatever small thing is given in the month of Kārtika dedicated to Viṣṇu, / all of that becomes inexhaustible; this is the truth spoken by me.
Whoever gives a betel leaf smeared with ghee to a Vaiṣṇava in the month of Kārtika, / day after day, O brāhmaṇa, his residence is in Viṣṇu's city.
Whoever worships the Beloved of Kamalā with a blooming lotus leaf, white or blue, / what is hard for him to obtain on earth?
By which foremost twice-born a lotus is not offered to Hari in the month of Kārtika, / what has been given by him, O brāhmaṇa, to Viṣṇu, conqueror of the Daityas?
Having brought even a single lotus, he gives it to the foe of Kaiṭabha; / what does the blessed Lord Viṣṇu, the Husband of Śrī, not give to him?
By whoever Hari is not worshipped with lotuses in the month of Kārtika, / birth after birth, Kamalā does not abide in his house.
Whoever offers lotus seeds to high-souled Keśava / is born into a pure brāhmaṇa family in every birth.
Born in a family of brāhmaṇas, he becomes a friend of the four Vedas, / wealthy, having many sons, and a sustainer of relatives.
There is no flower equal to the lotus; O Jaimini, it is spoken truly: / by worshiping Govinda with it, even an evil soul partakes of liberation.
The glorification of the lotus flower will be related by me in particular; / listen attentively, O best of the twice-born, along with its legendary history.
There was a certain brāhmaṇa named Prajāna, who knew all the śāstras, / the bee of whose mind ever remained in Hari's lotus feet.
Worship of the gods, brāhmaṇas, and gurus was always performed by him, / O best of the twice-born, alongside hundreds of duties and actions.
Another's wealth was [regarded by him] as poison, and other men's wives as his own mother; / thus it was done by him indeed, and likewise toward friend and foe.
Seeing a guest arriving, that brāhmaṇa, who knew the supreme truth, / never felt arrogance toward a beggar or an excellent twice-born.
All sacrifices were performed by him, and all vows, / desiring to cross over the terrible, fathomless ocean of saṃsāra.
Once that best of the twice-born, devoted to devotion to Hari, / contemplated in his mind his own death and his own birth:
"Who was I standing previously? Or what deed was done in the past? / How was this birth obtained? Or where shall I go again?"
Having reflected thus and sighing again and again, that twice-born / went indeed to the sacred site of Śiva in order to learn of his former deeds.
There, folding his hands in reverence and endowed with supreme devotion, / the brāhmaṇa praised the god Śaṅkara, Śiva, with sweet speech.
The brāhmaṇa said: / "Salutations to you, O Mahādeva! Salutations to you, O Parameśvara! / Salutations to you, O Śaṅkara, O Īśāna! Salutations to you, O Lord who grant boons!
Salutations to you whose form is knowledge! Salutations to you who bestow knowledge! / Salutations to you who dwell in the heart-lotus of all living beings!
Salutations to you, creator of the universe! Salutations, salutations to the father of the universe! / Salutations to the agent of dissolution, and salutations to the lord of creatures!
Salutations to you whose eye is fire! Salutations to you who look with fire! / Salutations to you whose eye is the moon! Salutations indeed to you whose eye is the sun!
Salutations to you adorned with ashes! Salutations to you dressed in an animal hide! / Salutations to you wearing a garland of bones! Salutations indeed to you with a blue throat!
Salutations to you with five faces! Salutations to you who hold a trident in hand, / who shatter the pride of Kāmadeva, possessing a formidable form!
Salutations to the God of gods! Salutations to the enemy of Tripura! / To the lord of Pārvatī, salutations to you of formidable form!
Salutations to you whose mind was deeply pleased by the devotion of Bāṇa! / Salutations indeed to you who have many forms! Salutations indeed to you who have all forms!
Salutations indeed to you who bear the Gaṅgā, the destroyer of Dakṣa's sacrifice! / To the lord of spirits, salutations to you who wield the Pināka bow!

Salutations to Īśāna! Salutations, salutations to Wisdom! / Salutations be to you who are visible! Salutations to you who are invisible! / Salutations indeed to you who are conceivable! Salutations to you who are inconceivable!
You alone are Brahmā, the sole lord of the gods; you alone are Viṣṇu; you alone are the sun; / you alone are the moon, the remover of all distress! Salutations, salutations to you, O Parameśvara!"
Hearing his hymn of praise, Śaṅkara, the bringer of auspiciousness to the world, / the gracious Parameśvara, suddenly became manifest.
Beholding him appeared, worshiped by all the gods, / that brāhmaṇa, endowed with immense devotion, bowed to his feet.
Again, with a mind filled with joy, that best of the twice-born, / folding his hands in reverence, praised Mahādeva, the boon-granting Lord.
The brāhmaṇa said: / "The Lord of gods whom even the gods with Indra do not behold, / him I see face to face—this is my great good fortune!
The Parameśvara who is invisible [even] to a mind fixed in meditation, / him I see face to face; what else remains for me to achieve?
Merely by remembering your name, even perpetrators of great sins / go to the supreme abode; I look upon that Lord [himself]!
I have attained my goal, I have attained my goal, I have attained my goal and am fortunate! / Salutations to you, salutations to you! Be pleased, O Parameśvara!"

Mahādeva said: / "I am pleased with this utterance of yours, O best of the twice-born! / Choose a boon, O fortunate one; I indeed wish to give a boon."

The brāhmaṇa said:
"You, the Supreme Self, invisible even to the gods, / I behold directly, O Lord; what need is there of other boons?"
Even so, O Mahādeva, full of compassion, you desire to give a boon; / tell me that which I ask, O Parameśvara:
Who was I living in the past, O God? Or what deed was done formerly? / How have I fallen into the ocean of saṃsāra, O Lord, O Master?
Through karma a body is obtained; the embodied soul is smeared by sin; / again by the influence of sin a terrible destiny is obtained.
By the power of which deeds has this birth been obtained by me, / which bestows various sufferings, O Lord? Being pleased, tell me, O Śaṅkara!
This birth is rooted in sin, and birth is the cause of suffering; / therefore I desire to know my own past history.
Tormented by the stomach's fire, I remained in my mother's womb, / strewn with urine and feces, by the ripening of my actions.
No suffering equal to dwelling in the womb is known in saṃsāra; / how was that experienced by me, O Lord, destroyer of the distress of devotees?
In this exceedingly terrible saṃsāra, full of diverse sufferings, / unsubstantial, deluded by the māyā of Viṣṇu, the resort of sins,
difficult to cross, devoid of kinsmen, connected with desire, anger, and the like, / giving grief and disease, and bestowing birth and death,
fathomless—how have I fallen [into it], O Lord of the worlds, O Śiva? / Tell me all this, O all-pervading Lord, if there is favor toward me."
Mahādeva said: / "Although this is greater than the greatest secret, O best of the twice-born, / and not to be disclosed, yet I shall tell it to you, my devotee.
Formerly you, an excellent brāhmaṇa [now], were born in the lineage of Śabaras; / renowned as Daṇḍapāṇi, you lived causing suffering to people.
Abandoning fear of the other world, devoid of discrimination, / you resorted to the occupation of a robber, which causes supreme affliction to the distressed.
Seeing you taking to the life of a robber and being extremely cruel, / all your other brothers also became robbers.
I shall declare the names of those brothers, O lord among twice-born, / with which brothers banditry was committed by you formerly:
Daṇḍī, Daṇḍāyudha, Dattavān, Dattabhū, / Sundaḍa, and Daṇḍaketu—six brothers are proclaimed.
With those most terrible brothers, completely bereft of compassion, / by your staff all people were perpetually harassed.
Out of greed for wealth, along with those wicked brothers, / in the forest and desolate wilderness, O brāhmaṇa, hundreds and thousands were killed [by you].
Having slain them with sharp arrows while staying in the forest, O twice-born, / the flesh of cows was always eaten by you along with intoxicating spirits.
Then, out of fear of you, all merchants abandoned the practice of traveling; / thus disaster perpetually befell that forest.
When you took to robbery, he who had wealth had no wealth; / he who had a house had no house; he who had a wife had no wife.
In this way, in that very great forest with those brothers of yours, / [one day,] exhausted from the fatigue of traveling, [you] went to a lake to bathe.

Having bathed there, O best of brahmins, being hungry,
lotus stalks and water were consumed by those brothers.

Then, O best of brahmins, O excellent one, out of playful curiosity,
many blossoming lotus flowers were eaten there by you.

At that very time, a brahmin dwelling in the forest,
known as Sarvavedas, arrived there to bathe.

Having bathed there, that righteous soul, endowed with humility,
begged of you a single lotus to worship the blessed Janārdana.

Then, O leader of brahmins, a single spotless lotus was given
by you with supreme devotion for the worship of the lord of Kamalā.

Pleased with the lotus given by you, that best of brahmins
worshiped Viṣṇu, the creator of all, right there.

Seeing that brahmin, Sarvavedas, intent on the worship of Viṣṇu,
you too, smiling, bowed down to Viṣṇu who grants all desires.

Then, having worshiped the supreme Self who grants the fruit of the four aims of life
according to the prescribed rules, that brahmin departed just as he had come.

By that gift of a lotus, by that bow, O excellent one,
and by witnessing the worship of Viṣṇu, all your sin was destroyed.

Then, after some days in that very great forest,
your time having arrived, you underwent death, O best of brahmins.

Satisfied by that very deed, the Blessed One, the abode of compassion,
gave you that supreme abode very difficult to obtain even for the gods.

For thousands of manvantaras and hundreds of manvantaras,
various pleasures were enjoyed there through the grace of the lord of Kamalā.

Then, at the end of that karma, having come to this land of works, O brahmin,
through those fruits of merit you were born in a brahmin lineage.

Having obtained birth in a pure brahmin family, O excellent one,
you obtained unswerving devotion to Hari, the refuge of all virtues.

The Lord, the great Viṣṇu, has been propitiated by you through practical yoga;
He will grant you knowledge; through knowledge you will be liberated.

Go, O brahmin—auspiciousness unto you—well-pleased, to your own house;
you have attained the sight of Me; you are liberated from the bonds of worldly existence.

Then for three days he worshiped Viṣṇu with charming lotus flowers
with great effort, to praise the supreme Lord.

Having worshiped Viṣṇu for a long time with wondrous, beautiful lotus blossoms, and having fallen asleep,
he attained knowledge and went to liberation by the grace of the Lord whose banner bears Garuḍa.

Such is the fruit for one who gives a lotus even unintentionally;
for one who gives [it] with devotion to Viṣṇu, I know not what it may be!

It is true, true, and true again—truly is it spoken by me:
having worshiped Hari with lotuses, the supreme abode is attained.

He who offers even a single lotus to the enemy of Mura,
for him there is no rebirth in terrifying transmigrations.

Those who worship Nārāyaṇa, full of compassion and granter of desires, with blooming lotuses
even for a single day, even sinners endowed with heinous sins, go toward liberation.

7.14.m:
Vyāsa said:
In the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, O best of brahmins, a Vaiṣṇava should worship
the imperishable Viṣṇu accompanied by Mahālakṣmī with a devotional disposition.

In a barbarian land, O leader of brahmins, likewise in the house of a fallen person,
and in a place permeated by foul smells, one should not worship Viṣṇu.

Near heretics, and likewise near great sinners,
and near those who speak falsehood, one should never worship Viṣṇu.

Nor should one perform the worship of Hari in the presence of those who are lamenting,
those who are quarreling, or in a place where people mock.

One should not worship Viṣṇu in a place of those addicted to receiving gifts,
nor in the house of misers who desire the wealth of others.

Likewise, one should not perform the worship of Viṣṇu [in the place] of deceitful persons.
In the worship of Nārāyaṇa, O brahmin, one should be wholly dedicated to devotion.

Casting aside any distracted mind, one should be intent upon meditating on Hari;
[with] crying of 'Alas!', sighing, and amazement, O best of brahmins,

or conversation with heretics, one should not worship Hari.
Having become single-minded toward the God of gods, the teacher of the world,

whatever flower is offered, even in ashes, reaches Hari;
[yet] one exhausted by hundreds of arriving anxieties, O brahmin, even upon Śālagrāma stones,

whatever flower that mortal gives, the Lord does not receive it.
Having become single-minded, the wise man should worship Viṣṇu with devotion.

Whatever deed is performed with an agitated mind is fruitless;
every deed is subject to the mind, and the three worlds are subject to the mind.

Therefore, having steady the mind, one should worship the lord of Kamalā.
He whose worship is in one place and whose mind is elsewhere, O best of brahmins,

even in hundreds of millions of kalpas his deed will not bear fruit.
Though he has diligently performed purification, and though he is intent on the worship of Viṣṇu,

if he is devoid of purity of mind, he is regarded as merely an outcaste.
Whatever austerity is performed without devotion for a very long time according to the rules, O brahmin,

it all becomes useless, merely a mortification of the body.
Gold the size of Mount Meru, given to a brahmin householder

without devotion, to dispel entreaty or even for one's own welfare, [is useless].
Therefore, having become single-minded, endowed with devotion and faith,

one should offer greens such as vāstuka in an assembly of Vaiṣṇavas.
He who offers a divine, well-ripened orange fruit

to Keśava, O best of brahmins, he is revered by us.
With effort, whatever new item is dear to the blessed Hari,

that very thing one should give with devotion to the enemy of Mura in the month of Āgrahāyaṇa.
When the month of Pauṣa arrives, [to] the Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the boon-granting Lord,

the Vaiṣṇava should bathe the God with divine sugarcane juices.
Whoever bathes the Lord Viṣṇu with sugarcane juices, O leader of brahmins,

enjoys all happiness in this world, and, when dead, goes to the ocean of sugarcane juice.
Whoever offers an oblation of sugarcane to Viṣṇu, the God of gods,

he too attains that fruit; what need of many words?
Having given flattened rice with good milk or with curds in Pauṣa

to the enemy of Mura, a mortal obtains all desires.
Having removed the old garment along with everything else, for the enemy of Mura,

in order to ward off cold, one should offer a new garment.
At the winter solstice of Pauṣa, O brahmin, to Viṣṇu who is accompanied by Lakṣmī,

a person desiring liberation should offer a seat of ten colors.
Whoever produces the sound of a conch after worshiping the lord of Kamalā,

I shall tell the meritorious fruit of that; listen attentively, my child:
freed from all sins such as incestuous union with forbidden women,

at the end he goes to the city of Viṣṇu and rejoices with Viṣṇu.
Whoever rings a bell marked with Garuḍa for Hari

at the time of worship, O best of brahmins, I tell his merit:
freed from all sins such as eating forbidden food,

he ascends a splendid chariot and goes to the abode of Viṣṇu.
Having enjoyed all desires there for a period of hundreds of millions of kalpas,

having returned to the earth as a best of brahmins versed in the four Vedas,
he enjoys all desires there for a period of hundreds of millions of kalpas.
Going once more to the city of Viṣṇu, he attains unsurpassed liberation. / But whoever plays the lute at the time of worship of the Lord of the world
that mortal becomes the foremost of scholars in every birth. / Whoever plays the mṛdaṅga drum during the worship of the enemy of Kaiṭabha,
the blessed Lord, well-pleased, gives him his desired fruit. / Likewise, whoever plays the ḍamaru, the ḍiṇḍima, the jharjharī, the madhurī,
the kettle-drum, the dundubhi drum, the kāhala, the sindhuvāraka, / the bell-metal gong, the cymbals, and the flute
at the time of the worship of Mahāviṣṇu—hear of his merit! / Freed from sins [such as those] incurred for theft, he goes to the dwelling of the wielder of the discus;
having attained supreme knowledge, he is liberated right there. / Whoever makes the kala sound at the time of the worship of the teacher of the world
and plays mouth-music, O best of Brahmins, of his merit it is said by me: / together with crores upon crores of family members, he proceeds to the dwelling of Hari;
having attained knowledge right there, he reaches imperishable liberation. / Whoever, filled with devotion, dances in Viṣṇu's temple,
he goes, O best of Brahmins, to that supreme abode of Viṣṇu. / But whoever sings songs with devotion before Nārāyaṇa,
he attains kingship among the cities of the Gandharvas. / And a Vaiṣṇava person who praises the Lord of the world with hymns in devotion,
the blessed Lord, pleased with him, grants all his desires. / Whoever worships Hari month by month by this rule,
that Acyuta is pleased with him without delay, O Brahmin sage.

Those mortals who wish to cross over this ocean of worldly existence, which is exceedingly deep and the cause of all sorrows— / let them all worship the two charming lotus feet of the Supreme Person, which are attended by hosts of the gods.

7.15.m: Vyāsa said: / I speak again of the glorification of Nārāyaṇa; listen, O twice-born! / Hearing which, a human being is freed from all sins.
This entire universe has become a portion of Viṣṇu, O best of Brahmins; / therefore, the wise who seek the supreme reality see it as consisting of Viṣṇu.
Brahmā, Śaṅkara, Rudra, and the others—all the gods are portions of Viṣṇu; / therefore, the worship of all gods goes to Viṣṇu alone.
For those who remember the names of Viṣṇu, which remove all sins, / by any means whatsoever, misfortune nowhere exists.
All sin indeed, O best of Brahmins, is eradicated through ritual action; / this remembrance of Viṣṇu is the imperishable destroyer of sins.
Sleeping, eating, speaking, standing, rising, and walking, / a Vaiṣṇava person who is a seeker of liberation should remember Viṣṇu without ceasing.
By all the exalted sages, no rule of time has been stated / for the remembrance of the husband of Kamalā, which destroys all sorrow.
The power of the name of the great-souled Keśava / I tell in brief, along with an itihāsa; listen to it, O Brahmin sage!
In the Kṛta age there was formerly a pure man named Saparaśu, / a Vaiśya, the best of the Vaiśya lineage, who had mastered all virtues.
By the power of fate, O Brahmin, that Vaiśya in his prime of youth / fell under the power of death, afflicted by the disease of cough and shortness of breath.
His wife, slender-waisted and in the bloom of youth, was named Jīvantī; / her husband having died, she went to her father's house.
That Jīvantī, O best of Brahmins, arrogant with the bloom of youth, / took to lovers, even though restrained by her kinsmen.
Vows and observances, and household work as well— / she whose mind was attached to paramours abandoned them in the bloom of youth.
Blinded by lust, with fine hips and full breasts, / she never saw the path of dharma, O best of Brahmins.
Seeing her ill-behaved, her father, devoted to dharma, / terrified by the fear of infamy, said to her with great wrath:
"O wicked one, O sinner! In my lineage, which is free of all defects, / having attained birth, why is sin committed by you?
If your mind is set on sin, do not come here to eat; / O inauspicious woman, go from this house! Leave my dwelling!'
Addressed thus by her father, her eyes reddened with rage, / she abandoned her father's home and went as she pleased.
Then, wandering at will in longing for lovers, / that woman took to the profession of a courtesan and lived devoid of shame.
Whether a Pulinda, a Śabara, or a Cāṇḍāla came to her house, / that unchaste woman sporting with him with delight.
O Brahmin, never in her mind did that courtesan / think of the fear of the other world, in due course.
Once, O best of Brahmins, a certain hunter came to her house / bringing a young parrot in order to sell it.
That courtesan also, honoring the hunter with money, / took that excellent young parrot with the greatest affection.
By giving food suitable for it, that courtesan continually / nurtured the parrot, her curiosity awakened towards it.
Childless, that courtesan looked after it / as her own son, and raised that very young parrot.
That bird also, O best of Brahmins, by her direction constantly / displayed the affectionate behavior of a kinsperson from the heart.
Then that parrot, having won her love, was regularly taught / the name 'Rāma', consisting of beautiful syllables, by the courtesan.
The name Rāma is the supreme Brahman, greater than all gods, great, / the destroyer of all sins; and that parrot was reciting it constantly.
By the mere utterance of 'Rāma', the very dreadful sin / of both of them, the parrot and the courtesan, was destroyed.
At a certain time, O best of Brahmins, that prominent courtesan / and the parrot both met their death at the very same time.
Then, to bring those two who had committed all sins, / Dharmarāja dispatched his servants, Caṇḍa and the others.
Then all those servants, Caṇḍa and the rest, exceedingly swift, / arrived by Yama's order, with nooses and clubs in their hands.
When they came to take the two, they saw all the attendants of Viṣṇu / who had arrived, possessing Viṣṇu's prowess, seeing the two bound with nooses and fallen down.
Angry, they spoke this word to Yama's messengers, who were formidable to gods:
The messengers of Viṣṇu said: / 'Ah, strange is this statement heard from the mouth of Yama's messengers!
Even these two devotees of Hari are to be punished by the son of the Sun? / Ah, the conduct of the wicked is never good!
For even with effort they constantly do harm to the virtuous. / Strange is this conduct of the wicked who have committed sins!
Meritorious souls see the entire world as free of sin; / but sinners do not see it as anything but full of sin committed.
Righteous people are fully satisfied upon hearing of the merit of meritorious souls; / sinful people are satisfied upon hearing of the sin of sinners.
Just as sinners are satisfied upon hearing a talk of sins, / they are not satisfied even having obtained hundreds of loads of gold.
Ah, powerful is the māyā of the great-souled Mahāviṣṇu, / [by which] they commit sin, O Brahmin, even though it causes torment to themselves!'
Vyāsa said: / Having spoken thus, those messengers of Viṣṇu, devoted to the worship of Viṣṇu, / cut the bonds of both of them with the edge of the discus, O Brahmin.
Then the servants of Yama, enraged and resembling fire, / suddenly rained down masses of burning charcoal there.
Daṇḍa said: / "Even by me it was ordained: you have come to carry off the parrot and the sinful prostitute! / This is quite astonishing.
If indeed you best of beings wish to carry off these two, / then fight with us right now!"
Having spoken thus, those mighty messengers of Rāma, holding weapons, / all arrogant, filled the directions with lion-roars.
The noble servants of Viṣṇu, Supratīka and the others, / then filled the world with sound by the delightful blasts of their conchs.
Then those messengers of Viṣṇu were covered in that exceedingly fierce battle / by arrows discharged from bows by the great messengers of Yama.
Some hurled tridents, some hurled a spear into the great throng; / some in anger [hurled] thousands of arrows, and others discs.
With maces, weapons and other means, those servants of Viṣṇu, great warriors, / pulverized the arrows and the great missiles discharged by them.
Then, by the edge of the discs of those devotees of the Lord, / the feet of some of Yama's servants were severed, and likewise the arms of others.
Some had their heads severed, some had their chests pierced through; / some with extraordinary wounds, the servants of Yama fell, lifeless.
Some with one foot severed, some with one hand severed, / suddenly abandoning the battle, the servants of Yama fled.
Seeing those messengers bent on flight, / Caṇḍa, bearing a club, entered into battle in fury.
The foremost of Yama's host of messengers, Caṇḍa, of immense prowess, / struck the attendants of Viṣṇu by the hundreds with his club.
Then the messengers of the Lord, infuriated, swiftly showered / fierce Caṇḍa with showers of sharpened weapons.
Then Caṇḍa, his body bathed in flowing blood, / struck the messengers of Viṣṇu one by one with his club.
Those messengers of the Lord, struck in battle by Caṇḍa, / lost their courage and retreated behind Suprakāśa.
Then Suprakāśa, enraged, his eyes resembling the hibiscus flower, / mace in hand and of great strength, entered into the fight in battle.
Furious and equal in prowess to Viṣṇu, he struck [the club] / from Caṇḍa's hand, looking upon that club that caused dread to people.
From that club, struck with force by fierce [Suprakāśa], / there arose something exceedingly dreadful, smoky, and foul-smelling.
It instantly emitted a shower of sparks that caused extreme terror. / Then this enraged Caṇḍa, with that very club,
struck the mighty Suprakāśa, O brahmin sage. / Then, O brahmin, Suprakāśa, enraged, forgetting the pain,
struck Caṇḍa, the servant of Yama, with his mace. / Struck by him, Caṇḍa was bathed in blood there,
and fell to the ground unconscious, like the young sun, O Jaimini. / Then those messengers of Yama, picking up the unconscious Caṇḍa,
fled in terror from the battle, uttering wails of grief. / Then all the messengers of Viṣṇu were exceedingly delighted, O brahmin;
they blew their conchs, O Jaimini, best of twice-born. / Then those messengers of Yama, drenched in torrents of blood,
went into the presence of Yama, weeping and overcome with fear.
The messengers of Yama said: / "O mighty-armed son of the Sun, we carry out your orders; / even so, such a wretched condition has been inflicted on us by the messengers of Viṣṇu!
Though those two were surely the foremost among great sinners, O Lord, / through the power of the name of Rāma they have gone to the abode of Nārāyaṇa.
Those wicked people who have committed sins ought to be punished by you; / if even they go to the city of Viṣṇu, then what is your authority?
This humiliation was not inflicted upon us by the messengers of Viṣṇu; / it was upon you alone, O master, since we are only your servants!"
Yama said: / "O messengers, since those two remembered the two syllables of the name 'Rāma, Rāma', / then they were not to be punished by me; Nārāyaṇa is their master.
There is no sin in worldly existence that does not instantly perish / even through recollections of Rāma; listen firmly, O servants!

Those men who daily remember with devotion the names of Madhusūdana, / which destroy hosts of terrible sins, and who is worshipped by the foremost of the gods— / even if they are sinners, O soldiers, they are not to be punished by me.

Men on earth who constantly utter with devotion: / 'Govinda, Keśava, Hari, Lord of the Universe, Viṣṇu, Nārāyaṇa, Tender to the suppliant, Mādhava!'— / they are not to be punished, O my soldiers, even if they are great sinners.

Men on earth who constantly say: / 'Destroyer of the distress of devotees, Lord of gods, Friend of the helpless, Consort of Lakṣmī, Cause of the destruction of all sins!'— / even if they are sinners, O soldiers, they are not to be punished by me.

'Dāmodara, One served by the hosts of gods headed by the Lord, Glorious Vāsudeva, Highest Puruṣa, Mādhava!'— / those in whose mouths these words always sound, / O messengers, I bow to them every single day.

Men whose thoughts are affectionate toward discourse about Nārāyaṇa, / Murāri, the sole Lord of the universe, / I am always subject to them, O noble soldiers, who possess forms like the blooming lotus-eyed Lord.

Those devoted to the worship of Viṣṇu, devotees of Hari's devotees, / intent on the vow of Ekādaśī, free from deceit, / who carry the water from Viṣṇu's feet upon their heads— / even if they are sinners, O soldiers, they are not to be punished by me.

Those who consume the remnants of the food offerings to the Lord Madhusūdana, / which destroy all masses of sins, / and who constantly bear on their ears and head the leaves of the Tulasī— / O soldiers, I bow down to them.

Those intent on worshipping the lotus-feet of Kṛṣṇa, / devoted to worshipping brāhmaṇas and honoring virtue, / who give extreme happiness to the hearts of the distressed— / I am always subject to them, O soldiers.

Those ever devoted to speaking truthful words, / dear to people, protectors of those who seek refuge, / and who constantly regard another's property like poison— / those men, O my soldiers, are indeed not to be punished.

Those devoted to the gift of food, givers of water, / givers of land, wishing welfare to all the world, / tranquil, satisfying those who have lost their livelihood— / O messengers, they are never to be punished.

Those devoted to supporting their kin, speaking kindly, / whose minds are free from hypocrisy, anger, arrogance, and malice, / who are free from sinful gaze and have conquered their senses— / I never even initiate inquiry about them."
Vyāsa said: / Instructed thus by Yama, the servants of Yama / came to know the matchless power of Hari, the sustainer of the world.
The names of Viṣṇu, O best of twice-born, are indeed superior to all the gods; / and among them, the knowers of truth remember the name of Rāma as the best.
The two syllables 'Rā-ma' are indeed superior to all mantras, O twice-born; / by their mere utterance, even a sinner attains the highest state.
The power of the name of Rāma is indeed the worship of all the gods; / Maheśa alone knows it, and no one else knows it, O Jaimini.
The fruit one obtains from reciting the thousand names of Viṣṇu, / that very fruit a mortal obtains even by remembering the name of Rāma.
Ah, how wonderful is this conduct of mortals that is spoken of: / evil-minded people do not remember the name "Rāma," which bestows liberation!
It requires not even the slightest effort to speak, and it is exceedingly delightful to hear; / nevertheless, evil-minded people do not say, "Rāma, Rāma!"
Though liberation is attained in this world by human beings only with extreme difficulty, / it is attained by the mere name of Rāma. What rite could be superior to this?
Sins dwell in the bodies of embodied beings, O best of men, / only so long as they indeed do not remember "Rāma, Rāma," which bestows happiness.
In the ancestral rite and the water offering, in making food offerings and likewise at a festival, / in sacrifice, charity, and observances, and even in worshipping deities,
and also in other Vedic duties, a wise person / who, desiring the fruit thereof, remembers "Rāma, Rāma" with devotion,
and whoever repeats the six-syllable mantra preceded by Oṃ, "Obeisance to Rāma," O chief of Brahmins, / attains communion with Hari.
A person who performs the worship of Hari with this six-syllable mantra / attains all desires through the grace of the wielder of the discus.
Whoever remembers "Rāma, Rāma" at the time of death, O best of the twice-born, / that person, even if most sinful, attains supreme liberation.
Wise men who remember the name "Rāma" when on a journey / attain complete success on their journey; there is no doubt about this.
Whoever remembers the name of Rāma in a forest or an open wilderness, / or in a dreadful cremation ground, no misfortunes are found for him, O twice-born.
At the king’s court and in a difficult fortress, in a foreign land, when facing robbers, / upon having bad dreams, and during planetary afflictions, O Jaimini,
and in fear caused by natural portents or fear of diseases caused by wind humor, / a mortal who remembers the name of Rāma incurs nothing inauspicious anywhere.
The name of Rāma, O best of the twice-born, averts all inauspicious things; / granting desires and granting liberation, it must be remembered constantly by the wise.
In whichever moment the name "Rāma" is not remembered, O Brahmin sage, / that moment alone becomes useless; this truth is proclaimed by me.
Mortals do not sink into despair when remembering the names of Hari.

A mortal who desires the destruction of sins committed across ten million births and attains prosperity on earth / has constantly remembered the name of Viṣṇu on earth with devotion, which bestows liberation and is exceedingly sweet.

7.16.m: Vyāsa said: / Once again, O best of the twice-born, I shall proclaim the glory / of the Supreme Self, Mahāviṣṇu, which destroys all suffering; listen!
Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, Śūdras, and others born of the lowest classes / who have taken refuge in devotion to Hari are fulfilled; there is no doubt.
Even a Brahmin devoid of devotion to Hari is to be known as worse than an outcaste dog-cooker; / even an outcaste dog-cooker who is devoted to Hari is to be known as superior to a Brahmin.
How can he be a Brahmin who is devoid of devotion to Hari? / How can he be an outcaste dog-cooker whose mind is dedicated to devotion to the Lord?
When Viṣṇu is worshipped without deceit even by an outcaste dog-cooker, / then one should see even him as superior to a twice-born master of the four Vedas.
Formerly, in the age called Dvāpara, there was a Śabara named Cakrika, / an oppressor of people, devoid of the proper conduct of a noble caste.
Yet he did not dispute with Brahmins; he conquered anger, refrained from violence toward others, / was compassionate, free from hypocrisy, and devoted to his mother and father.
He did not engage in conversations with Vaiṣṇavas, nor had he heard the treatises on liberation; / nevertheless, unshakeable devotion to Hari arose in his heart.
"O Hari, O Keśava, O Govinda, O Vāsudeva, O Janārdana!" / Thus he constantly remembered the names of the wielder of the discus.
Whatever wild fruit he obtained, O best of the twice-born, / that descendant of the Śabaras first placed into his own mouth.
Having then ascertained its sweetness, he would take it out of his mouth again / and give it to Hari with devotion, well-pleased, every day.
Whether it was tasted leavings or untouched food, he understood neither distinction at all; / for the inherent nature of one's own caste always rests on one's head.
Once, wandering in the interior of the forest, O best of the twice-born, / having obtained a single ripe fruit of a priyāla tree,
then Cakrika, delighted at finding that fruit, / having quickly examined it, placed it inside his own mouth.
As soon as he placed that fruit inside his own mouth, O twice-born, / that fruit entered his throat; listen, O Jaimini!
Then, with his left hand, he held tight the cavity of his throat; / carefully grasping it with his left hand, O twice-born,
Cakrika, devoted to the worship of Hari, thought: / "If I do not give this fruit to that foe of Mura,
then no sinner like me has ever been born in this worldly cycle." / Having thought of Hari in many ways, he then resolved his mind.
Nevertheless, that fruit did not emerge from his throat, O twice-born. / That single-minded devotee of Hari, having cut his throat with an axe
and brought forth that ripe fruit, offered it to the god Viṣṇu. / Approaching His presence, meditating on Him alone in his heart,
his entire body smeared with blood, he fell upon the surface of the earth. / Seeing that his life-breath had departed, the Blessed Lord Viṣṇu became distressed:
"No devotee equal to him exists for me, / since by cutting his own throat he has brought me satisfaction.
Just as this devotee has performed a sattvic deed, though of an altered nature, / what thing do I possess by giving which I may become free from debt to him?
Fortunate is he, exceedingly fortunate is he; he is blessed, there is no doubt here, / for even having abandoned his life-breaths, he brought me satisfaction.
Even if the state of Brahmā, the state of Śiva, or the state of Viṣṇu were given, / even then, discharge of debt to this devotee cannot indeed be attained."
Having spoken thus, the Blessed One who has Garuḍa on his banner, exceedingly pleased, / then touched his head with his lotus-like hand.
From the touch of His lotus hand, that Śabara, freed from pain, / of noble nature and devoted to Nārāyaṇa, stood up.
Vyāsa said: / Then Keśava wiped the dust from the limbs of this best of devotees with His own garment, / O twice-born, like a father to his son.
Beholding Janārdana visibly embodied, Cakrika, / bowing his head with folded hands, praised Him in sweet words.

Cakrika said: / "O Govinda, O Keśava, O Hari, O Lord of the Universe, O Viṣṇu, although I do not know words worthy of your praise, / nevertheless my tongue longs to praise you. O Master, be gracious; remove this great fault!

Abandoning you, O Lord of All, wielder of the discus, men on earth indeed worship another; / they alone are fools, the sole abode of a multitude of sins, because you are gracious even toward me, O God!

Although, O God, sole Lord of the world, one knows that it is only through devotion to you that the bond of existence of men is severed, / nevertheless, the Blessed Lord Viṣṇu is exceedingly gracious toward me, born in the lineage of Śabaras of utter sin.

The touch of whose charming lotus hand, O Lord, even the hosts of gods headed by the Four-faced One do not obtain— / that has been obtained today by me, a known [outcaste]; none is more compassionate toward his servants than you.

By you, the Blessed Lord, Kaṃsa the demon, the prime enemy of the thirty gods and son of Ugrasena, who committed all sins, / was formerly slain for the welfare of mortals and the host of immortals headed by Indra; obeisance to you, the bestower of supreme auspiciousness!"

By you, of immense might, the best of the gods, born of Vasudeva, the twin arjuna trees were felled, / and the wicked Kālayavana and Dhenuka were killed in battle; reverence be to you, who resemble a fresh cloud!

O Śrī Kṛṣṇa, O Dāmodara, O Ananta! By you the unwavering prosperity of the lord of the gods / was long ago established as the blessed Supreme Lord; reverence be to you, devoted to the lineage of Yadu!
Reverence and adoration to you, by whom the pārijāta tree was carried off, by whom the breaker of citadels [Indra] was vanquished, / and by whom the Great Lord [Śiva] was defeated in play!
Having made Vṛkodara the instrument, Jarāsandha was overthrown; / and the arms of the asura Bāṇa were struck down and slain by you.
Reverence, continuous reverence to you, by whom Śiśupāla was killed; / by you, the great-souled one, the burden of the earth was removed,
having slain the kṣatriyas through illusion; reverence, continuous reverence to you! / Vyāsa said: / When Viṣṇu had thus been praised by that great-souled Cakrika,
he was exceedingly pleased and said, 'Choose a boon, O Jaimini!' / Cakrika said: / 'O Supreme Brahman, O supreme abode, O supreme Self full of compassion!
I behold you directly; what need do I have of other boons, O twice-born one? / I did not meditate upon your form, nor did I perform your worship,
with food offerings, heavenly flowers, heavenly incense, or lamps; / nor were your names ever remembered by me.
The water of your feet, O master, was never held on my head; / your food offering was not eaten, nor was your vow performed by me.
Even so, I have beheld you; what should I do with other boons? / I was born in the lineage of the Śabaras, excluded from all duties;
even so, your lotus feet, which are difficult to attain even for the gods, / have today been obtained by me; what use do I have for other boons?
Even so, O beloved of Kamalā, if you wish to grant a boon, / may my mind abide in you, and never sink down, through your grace.'
The blessed Lord said: / 'O noble-minded one, through this shower of nectar of your words / great satisfaction has been attained by me, even toward a sinful servant.
Since this excellent lotus was offered to me by you, dear child, / I am exceedingly pleased with it, and, delighted, I accept your devotion.'
Vyāsa said: / Having spoken thus, the blessed Lord Viṣṇu, who accepts devotion and is full of compassion, / embraced that devotee with his four long arms.
The blessed Lord said: / 'I am pleased with your devotion, O child, best of Cakrikas! / Whatever is granted by me, dear one, will surely come to pass soon.'
Having embraced that great devotee once again, the Supreme Lord, / the Self of the universe and protector of the universe, vanished right there, O twice-born one.
That Cakrika, exceedingly pleased and intent on devotion to Hari, / abandoned his sons, wife, and all else, and went to the city of Dvārakā.
Arriving there in this manner, by the grace of the lord of Kamalā, / at the end of his life he attained liberation, which is hard to attain even for the gods.
Therefore, the deity is won over by the devotee and is satisfied by devotion alone; / not by hymns of praise, nor by wealth, nor by austerities, nor by recitation.
Even though a fruit that was leftover [food] was offered by him, O best of the twice-born, / Viṣṇu was nevertheless pleased, knowing his unswerving devotion.
Therefore, the god Nārāyaṇa should be [worshipped] in this worldly existence by seekers of liberation.
Those men who worship the pair of lotus feet of Vāsudeva— / which are worshipped by the foremost of the gods beginning with Vāsava—with firm devotion, indeed go to liberation.

7.17.m: Jaimini said: / 'Speak again, O guru, of the glorification of the lord of Kamalā! / Having drunk the nectar of Hari’s story, who could ever feel satiety?'
Glorious Vyāsa said: / 'No one in this world is virtuous like you, / since you wish to hear the glorification of Keśava with devotion.
The delightful story of Nārāyaṇa truly purifies the three worlds, / as well as the hearer, the questioner, and the speaker, O best of the twice-born.
Listen, my child, to the sin-destroying glorification of the lord of Lakṣmī; / I shall relate it concisely, bestowing the fruit of the four aims of life.
Whoever worships Viṣṇu with supreme devotion even for a single day, / Hari immediately destroys the sin accumulated by him over ten million births.
How can that mortal be a virtuous soul by whom Hari has not been worshipped? / And how can he be a sinner who has devotion to the Lord Nārāyaṇa?
There is a city, the best of all cities, named Puruṣottama, / endowed with all virtues and the refuge of the hosts of all the gods.
It is declared to be the foremost among all sacred places, / because Keśava resides directly in that delightful city.
There was formerly a certain twice-born man there named Bhadratanu, / handsome, sweet-speaking, and born of a pure family.
Having attained youth, the handsome twice-born man, infatuated by lust / and abandoning fear of the next world, became devoted to courtesans.
He did not study the Veda, nor the Purāṇas at all; / and he cast aside his good reputation due to association with heretics.
He accepted gifts from those not fit to sacrifice, robbed the wealth of others, / reviled dharma, and that twice-born man became intent on sin.
He abandoned brahminical conduct, as well as adherence to truth, / and the worship of teachers and guests—that vilest of brāhmaṇas.
Whatever action was more sinful, precisely that was performed; / and the most meritorious deed was never done by him, O Jaimini.
Once, full of fear and shame before the world, having committed sin, / that twice-born man indeed performed an ancestral rite, though devoid of faith in ancestral rites.
Having gone to her house at night, he spoke thus to the courtesan; / the brāhmaṇa said: / 'O woman of broad hips, today is the day of my ancestral rite;
yet, bound by your virtues, I have come to your abode. / Behold this night, O beloved, terrifying to everyone,
with a dense mass of leaking clouds covering the expanse of the sky! / On a path erased by fresh waters, my mind drawn by your virtues,
even in such a night I have arrived at your house, / driven by passion which, hostile to clouds and lightning, shows me my desire.
Trusting in meditation on your virtues, I have come at night, O darling; / without seeing you even for a moment, I find no joy.
Even with great distress, O slender one, I have come to see you; / what need do I have, O beloved, of sprinkling with the waters of sacred places?
Sprinkled with the water of the sacred ford of your love, I have attained heaven; / what fruit is there for me in worshipping an observance that yields happiness in the hereafter?
Even while living, heaven is attained by me through your grace; / out of fear of ill repute, O beloved, the ancestral rite was performed in my house.
In this ancestral rite not even the slightest faith of mine can be perceived; / you are my recitation, you are my austerity, and you are my morality, O beautiful one!
To you alone in this world, O beautiful one, with my whole being, / I have surrendered always; command me, what shall I do?'
The woman of slender waist said: / 'With you as a son, your father became truly sonless! / Even on the day of the ancestral rite, do you wish to engage in sexual intercourse?
O evil-minded one, whoever engages in sexual intercourse on the day of the ancestors, / his ancestors and he himself surely become eaters of semen.
If a fool, through delusion, engages in sexual intercourse on the day of the ancestors, / that ancestral offering becomes fit to be seized by rākṣasas; there is no doubt about this.'

What I have truly told you, if your mind were turned with such affection
towards Viṣṇu as it is toward me, what would it not attain?

The life of embodied beings stands within the staff of Yama,
yet even so, fool, you commit sin ever fearless.

The life of a fool is fleeting like a water bubble;
why, with the thought that it is eternal, do you always act perfidiously?

On whose forehead are written the two syllables 'mṛtyu' [death]—
how does he commit sin, which brings all suffering?

Ah, the illusion of Mahāviṣṇu is singularly powerful on earth,
since a twice-born, committing sin, is constantly joyful!

Sin has found a dwelling in my own body, an evil shelter;
indeed, it burns the hermitage like blazing fire burning wood.

Vyāsa said:
Spoken thus by the beautiful courtesan on account of his sin impelled by fate,
the brāhmaṇa who had committed sin reflected in his mind:

“Fie, fie upon me, a great sinner, a fool, the foremost among sinners!
The courtesan possesses that knowledge, whereas I, an evil-minded one, do not.

Having obtained birth in the pure family of a brāhmaṇa,
I have continually committed great sin that destroys the soul.

When death is certain once born, and when Yama is master when one dies,
how then do I commit sin out of lack of discrimination?

Muttering of prayers, austerities, oblations, and study of the Vedas,
the conduct of a priest, worship of guests, devotion to the guru, honoring twice-borns,

Rites such as ancestral offerings, and the worship of the lord of Kamalā—
I have performed none of these; from where will my supreme destination come?”

Bowing like a staff upon the ground, that twice-born with words
praised the great-souled Mārkaṇḍeya, the best of knowers of all duties.

The brāhmaṇa said:
“Salutations to you, O best of twice-borns! Long-lived one, salutations to you!
Salutations to you, the great-souled one, whose true form is Nārāyaṇa!”
Salutations to the son of Mṛkaṇḍa, who desires the welfare of all the worlds! / Salutations to you indeed, an ocean of knowledge, and truly immutable!
Praised thus by that brāhmaṇa, the greatly austere Mārkaṇḍeya, / who had reached the further shore of the meaning of all scriptures, spoke, supremely pleased.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / I am greatly pleased by your devotion, O fortunate one! Choose a boon; / I shall accomplish whatever you desire at once, not otherwise.
The brāhmaṇa said: / I am the foremost among sinful souls, devoid of the conduct of the twice-born, / ever engaged in violence toward others, always devoted to other men's wives.
By me, a fool, O chief of brāhmaṇas, great sin has always been committed; / not even in the next world has any merit ever been accrued with reverence.
In the terrible ocean of worldly existence, which gives misery and is exceedingly dreadful, / how can there be salvation for me, a great sinner?

Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Though having committed sins, O chief of brāhmaṇas, you are indeed the best among virtuous souls, / since such an understanding, difficult to obtain in worldly existence, has arisen in you.
The virtuous vision of virtuous souls increases day by day; / but the sinful vision of sinful souls increases day after day.
Even though you are a sinful soul, that sinful vision is being restrained; / therefore, the Lord of the World is clearly seen to be pleased with you.
Even after committing sin, the mortal who turns away from sin again— / they call him an exalted man, who worshipped Acyuta in a previous birth.
The Lord, Mahāviṣṇu, having seen His own devotee engaged in sin, / bestows abundant intellect so that a good destiny is attained.
Therefore, O best of brāhmaṇas, you have been a worshipper of Acyuta birth after birth; / before long, good fortune will be yours, without a doubt.
Whatever has been asked by you, O brāhmaṇa, you will not hear that from me; / because the time for my daily rites is now at hand.
There is a certain twice-born named Dānta, who knows the reality of all subjects; / he will tell you all of that; go to his hermitage.
Instructed by him, by the wise Mārkaṇḍeya, that brāhmaṇa / went quickly to Dānta's hermitage, which was pure and exceedingly beautiful,
adorned with aśvattha, campaka, bakula, and priyaka trees, / and with other blossoming trees, enchanting the mind,
with the fragrance of blooming flowers pervading the space between all quarters, / with swarms of humming bees, resounding with the sound of [falling] fruits,
with breezes blowing softly, and cool water, / frequented by hundreds of harmless beasts, crowded with disciples and sub-disciples.
Then, entering his exceedingly delightful hermitage, the brāhmaṇa / beheld Dānta, the knower of truth, surrounded by the hosts of all his disciples.
Having praised that best of brāhmaṇas, Dānta, who was one with Nārāyaṇa, / that best of the twice-born bowed to his feet with his head.
Dānta said: / Who are you, good sir, that have arrived? What is your purpose here? / Tell the truth: for what reason do you praise me now?
Bhadratanu said: / I am a brāhmaṇa, O fortunate one, devoid of a brāhmaṇa's conduct, / known by the name Bhadratanu, an agent of every wickedness.
How can there be a cutting off of the sins of worldly existence for me, a sinner? / Tell me this, O holy man, since you know the reality of all things.
Dānta said: / Listen, O brāhmaṇa, to the supreme secret which is spoken by me out of affection for you, / by which the cutting off of the noose of worldly existence comes to pass for men.
Abandon association with heretics; always cultivate the company of the good; / [abandon] desire, anger, delusion, greed, pride, and malice.
Abandon untruth and violence to others even with effort, O twice-born, / constantly remembering the names of the great-souled Mahāviṣṇu.
Sweeping, O best of the twice-born, and also smearing [with cow dung], / decorating the pathway, and placing a lamp—perform these in Keśava's temple.
Always perform service to brāhmaṇas and service to kin, / making gifts of food and water, and daily the five great sacrifices.
Hear the tale of Hari; repeat the twelve-syllable mantra; / as you perform all these deeds, O best of men,
supreme knowledge will arise; from knowledge you will attain liberation.
The brāhmaṇa said: / These things that have been spoken of by you as auspicious, O holy man— / tell their explanation: What are delusion, hypocrisy, and malice?
What is untruth, and what is violence? What are compassion, tranquility, and self-restraint? / And what is called equal vision? What is the worship of the Lord of Kamalā?
And what is called ahorātra? What is the remembrance of Viṣṇu? / What are the five great sacrifices, and what is the twelve-syllable mantra?
Tell the entire explanation of these, O best of brāhmaṇas, / so that by your grace I may attain the supreme state.
Dānta said: / Those who, having abandoned actions approved by the Veda, perform other acts, / and are devoid of their own proper conduct, are proclaimed to be heretics.
Those who hold fast to their own conduct, who perform what is approved by the Veda, / and are free from desire for sin, are proclaimed to be good men.
The desire which constantly exists for women, the acquisition of wealth, and the like, / O best of brāhmaṇas, is called desire.
The distress that arises in the heart upon hearing abuse of oneself, / that is to be known as anger, the destroyer of all righteousness.
The longing to take away another's wealth and property, which arises in the heart upon seeing it, / O best of the twice-born, is called greed.
'My mother, my father, this is my wife, [this is my] house'— / this other sense of 'mine' is called delusion.
'I am a great soul, wealthy, no one on earth is equal to me'— / this which arises in the mind is declared by the wise to be pride.
'People always censure me; fie upon my life!'— / one who speaks thus of oneself, that self-reproach is malice.
That speaking of truth which bestows happiness on all people, / that is to be known as truth; untruth is the opposite of that.
'When will this man's sovereignty, wife, sons, and the rest come to ruin?'— / such a thought arising in the mind is proclaimed to be violence.
The disposition of desire arising in the heart to remove another's suffering, / even with effort, O best of the twice-born, is proclaimed to be compassion.
The contentment that arises in the mind is spoken of as tranquility by the wise; / the non-restraint of the mind toward anything other than vile actions—
is proclaimed as self-restraint by the wise, approved by those who perceive truth. / In sorrow and in joy, O chief of brāhmaṇas, that contentment which remains always,

and likewise toward an enemy and a friend, is considered equal vision. / When a man worships Hari with devotion / using offerings of food, fragrances, flowers, and the like, O brāhmaṇa, that is proclaimed as worship.
The fasting that is observed at midday and at night—
eating on the preceding and following days—that is to be known as ahorātra. / The unification of both oneself and Keśava, / O best of men,
that is called the remembrance of Viṣṇu. / The sacrifice to Brahman, the sacrifice to men, the sacrifice to gods, O best of men,
the sacrifice to ancestors, and the sacrifice to spirits—these are proclaimed as the five sacrifices. / 'Oṃ namo bhagavate vāsudevāya', preceded by the Praṇava—
this the knowers of truth call the great twelve-syllable mantra. / Thus has all been told to you that was asked, O best of brāhmaṇas,
knowing which all human beings attain the supreme knowledge. / Therefore, every day, O brāhmaṇa, the one hundred and eight names...

[Mārkaṇḍeya said:]
“Having recited [this], you will attain liberation, which is hard to obtain, from the lord of Kamalā.”
Bhadratanu said:
“Tell me the hundred and eight names of Viṣṇu, the lord of Lakṣmī.”

The hundred and eight names that destroy great sins
should be recited having meditated [on him]. Listen to the meditation spoken by me:

Having the form of an atasī flower, with eyes like blooming lotuses,
his entire body adorned with the dust from the hooves of cows;

His noble head adorned with a band of cow-tail hair,
the Lord, whose charming pair of lips is placed upon the sound of the flute;

Surrounded by affectionate children dwelling in the cow-pen,
wearing yellow garments, with a lovely face: having meditated on the supreme face of Kṛṣṇa—

Salutations! Of this hymn of one hundred and eight names of Kṛṣṇa, the sage is Vedavyāsa, the meter is anuṣṭubh,
the deity is Śrī Kṛṣṇa; the application in repetition is for the pleasure of Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

Salutations: Kṛṣṇa, Keśava, Keśiśatru, Sanātana,
Kaṃsāri, Dhenukāri, Śiśupālaripu, Prabhu,

Devakīnandana, Śauri, Puṇḍarīkanibhekṣaṇa,
Dāmodara, Jagannātha, Jagatkartā, Jaganmaya,

Nārāyaṇa, Balidhvaṃsī, Vāmana, Aditinandana,
Viṣṇu, Yadukulaśreṣṭha, Vāsudeva, Vasuprada,

Ananta, Kaiṭabhāri, Mallajit, Narakāntaka,
Acyuta, Śrīdhara, Śrīmān, Śrīpati, Puruṣottama,

Govinda, Vanamālī, Hṛṣīkeśa, Akhilārtihā,
Nṛsiṃha, Daityaśatru, Matsyadeva, Jaganmaya,

Bhūmidhārī, Mahākūrma, Varāha, Pṛthivīpati,
Vaikuṇṭha, Pītavāsas, Cakrapāṇi, Gadādhara,

Śaṅkhabhṛt, Padmapāṇi, Nandakī, Garuḍadhvaja,
Caturbhuja, Mahāsattva, Mahābuddhi, Mahābhuja,

Mahotsava, Mahātejas, Mahābāhupriya, Prabhu,
Viṣvaksena, Śārṅgī, Padmanābha, Janārdana,

7.17.s:
tulasī vallabho'pāraḥ pareśaḥ parameśvaraḥ
paramakleśahārīcaparatrasukhadaḥ paraḥ
7.17.d:
तुलसी वल्लभोऽपारः परेशः परमेश्वरः
परमक्लेशहारीचपरत्रसुखदः परः
7.17.m:
Tulasīvallabha, Apāra, Pareśa, Parameśvara,
Paramakleśahārī, Paratrasukhada, Para,

Hṛdayastha, Ambarastha, Mohada, Mohanāśana,
Samastapātakadhvaṃsī, Mahābala, Balāntaka,

Rukmiṇīramaṇa, Rukmipratijñākhaṇḍana, Mahān,
Dāmabaddha, Kleśahārī, Govardhanadhara, Hari,

Pūtanāri, Muṣṭikāri, Yamalārjunabhañjana,
Upendra, Viśvamūrti, Vyomapāda, Sanātana,

Paramātmā, Parabrahma, Praṇatārtivināśana,
Trivikrama, Mahāmāya, Yogavid, Viṣṭaraśravas,

Śrīnidhi, Śrīnivāsa, Yajñabhoktā, Sukhaprada,
Yajñeśvara, Rāvaṇāri, Pralambaghna, Akṣaya, Avyaya.

This is the hundred and eight names out of the thousand names;
it brings all pleasure to Viṣṇu and destroys all sins.

It destroys bad dreams and removes affliction from planets;
it causes the destruction of all diseases and grants supreme sovereign power.

It destroys all afflictions and grants the fruit of all rites;
it has been proclaimed by me, O best of twice-borns, for the sake of the delight of Vaiṣṇavas.

Whoever constantly recites these one hundred and eight names with devotion at the three junctures of the day
in the presence of Hari—Hari is always pleased [with him].

And whatever devoted Vaiṣṇava recites this at a śrāddha,
his ancestors, being satisfied, proceed to the supreme abode.

Whoever recites it at the time of a sacrifice, in the worship of deities,
at the time of giving gifts, or on a journey, indeed obtains that fruit.

One without a son obtains a son; one seeking wealth obtains wealth;
one seeking learning obtains learning by chanting this praise.

For those who recite these one hundred and eight names with devotion to Hari,
there is never any misfortune on the face of the earth.

Dānta said:
“Go, O brāhmaṇa, may it be well with you! According to the rule spoken by me,
having fully worshipped Hari with devotion, you will attain supreme well-being.”

Having been thus instructed by that Dānta who was intent on the supreme goal,
he became devoted to the worship of Hari in that excellent holy place.

Constantly with devotion, O Jaimini, for five days that vipra
performed the worship of Hari according to the rite described by Dānta.

Knowing his devotion to be exceedingly firm, Hari, full of compassion,
manifested suddenly, radiant like ten million suns.

Seeing him, the lord of the worlds, the beloved of Kamalā, Acyuta,
the vipra bowed with his head at his two lotus-feet.

Then that best of brāhmaṇas, his mind filled with boundless joy,
with folded hands praised the lord of Kamalā, the lord of the universe:

“O Hari, you brought my gaze, though turned toward sin, to beneficial devotion to you, O merciful and all-pervading Lord!
Therefore, even though I had committed extensive sin, I was made like a cultured man by you today.

When you, whose two feet are praised by the gods, are angered, man’s gaze turns indeed to sin;
and when you are pleased, that very gaze turns toward virtue: this alone is known by me, O Supreme Lord!

I tell you, O Lord, such is the power of remembering you that, though I had accumulated every sin, I go;
he ascended a chariot inlaid with pure gold and went to the supreme abode obtainable only by the gods.”

7.17.d:
त्वत्पादपद्मसलिलस्यसदागुणाढ्योव्याधः सवेत्तिकनिकः कृतसर्वपापः
त्वद्वेश्ममार्जनफलंजगदेकनाथयज्ञध्वजः क्षितिपतिः सुरवंदितश्च
7.17.m: The hunter, though full of every sin, knows a drop of the water of your lotus feet, always rich in virtues; / and King Yajñadhvaja, praised by the gods, knows the fruit of sweeping your temple, O sole Lord of the world.

The fruit of plastering your temple, O Murāri, the Lord who is the cause of creation, maintenance, and dissolution, / is known by Yajñamālin, whose banner bears the enemy of serpents, and by his brother Sumālin, who feared his sins.
Whatever fruit there may be from circumambulating you, Hari, / Dharma alone knows it; no one else in the three worlds [knows].
Who on earth is able to declare your mind [and] your compassion, O Lord? / Even having pierced you with arrows, the hunter attained the supreme abode.
Even having reviled you, the Lord of the world, the master of the thirty [gods], / Śiśupāla went to liberation—what to say of your devotee?
By you, who in the form of Brahmā created this world— / in you, that Mahāviṣṇu, may my mind take delight.
All the destruction of the world is brought about by you, O Viṣṇu, / in the form of Rudra in this worldly existence; homage be unto that you from me.
Than whom there is nothing smaller, than whom there is nothing greater, / by whom, by you, this entire world is pervaded—homage be unto that you.
From whose two eyes the sun, maker of day, was born, / and from whose mouth fire is born—homage be unto that you, O god.
From whose ear even the winds and the life-breaths were born, O Keśava— / homage be always from me unto that you, O best of the gods.
Upon whose lap Lakṣmī always sits in great bliss, you whose limbs are dark, / like lightning upon a cloud—homage be unto that you.
To the limit of whose greatness even the immortals headed by Brahmā / are not able to go—homage be unto that you.
Who arises age after age for the sake of establishing dharmas / and for the destruction of sinners—homage be unto that you from me.
By whom, this great-souled one, this world is deluded through māyā, / [and] who, as Śambhu, destroys through māyā—homage be unto that you from me.
Who is pleased by devotion alone, not by wealth, nor by praises, / nor by gifts, nor by austerities—homage be unto that you from me.
Who acts for the welfare of cows, of brāhmaṇas, and of good people, / and bestows compassion—homage be unto that you from me.
The god who takes away the distress of the helpless, of kin, / of yogins, and of the afflicted—homage be unto that you from me.
Who abides with equality among humans, among gods, / and among all elephants—homage be unto that you from me.
When you are pleased, even a mountain instantly becomes like grass; / when you are angered, grass behaves like a mountain—homage be unto that you from me.
Just as the mind of the virtuous is set on merit, as a father's is on his own son, / and as that of chaste wives is on their husband, so indeed may mine be on you.
Just as the mind of the young is on women, as that of the greedy is on wealth, / and as that of the hungry is on food, so may mine be on you.
Just as that of those oppressed by heat is on the moon, of those oppressed by cold is on the sun, / and of those oppressed by thirst is on water, so indeed may mine be on you.
Whatever intercourse with the guru's wife was done by me devoid of sense— / may that sin perish as I look upon you.
Whatever killing of those who should not be killed was done by me possessed of delusion and illusion— / may that sin perish as I look upon you.
And whatever drinking of what should not be drunk was committed by me, O Supreme Lord— / may that sin perish as I look upon you.
Whatever emission of semen was made in the waters, in a non-vagina, and in water— / may that sin perish as I look upon you.
Whatever killing of an embryo was done, and emission of semen upon the ground— / may that sin perish as I look upon you.
And whatever betrayal of trust was done, out of ignorance [or] through delusion— / may that sin perish as I look upon you.
And whatever untruthful word was spoken by me at every moment— / may that sin perish as I look upon you.
Whatever censure of the virtuous was done, and injury to others at all times— / may that sin perish as I look upon you.
Whatever phlegm and mucus was discharged by me into the mouth [of another]— / may that sin perish as I look upon you.
Whatever felling of trees was done when Soma has entered the plants— / may that sin perish as I look upon you.
And whatever recitation of a root mantra was done on the road, in a temple, or in a cow-pen— / may that sin perish as I look upon you.
And whatever widespread lack of devotion toward father and mother [was shown], O Keśava— / may that sin perish as I look upon you.
Whoever was stopped while going to bathe or going to eat— / may that sin perish as I look upon you.
Whatever eating was done by me on the eleventh lunar day, O best of the gods— / may that sin perish as I look upon you.
A guest coming to the house was not honored by me, O Lord— / may that sin perish as I look upon you.
And whatever eating twice was done on the twelfth and on the tenth lunar days— / may that sin perish as I look upon you.
And whatever prevention was done to cows running to drink— / may that sin perish as I look upon you.
Whatever vow was begun by me and abandoned without completion— / may that sin perish as I look upon you.
Whatever false testimony was spoken by me out of affection for a friend— / may that sin perish as I look upon you.
Whatever failure there was to approach one's own wife at the proper season— / may that sin perish as I look upon you.
And whatever eating was done by me in an unconsecrated house— / may that sin perish as I look upon you.
And whatever practice of begging in villages was adopted by me, O Nṛhari— / may that sin perish as I look upon you.
Whatever exercise of power was done by me when the king was being punished, O Lord— / may that sin perish as I look upon you.
Whatever obstacle was caused by me in the middle of a story from the Purāṇas— / may that sin perish as I look upon you.
And whatever talk of another's cooking was eagerly listened to by me— / may that sin perish as I look upon you.
Whatever cutting down of the sacred fig tree and cutting down of the myrobalan tree was done— / may that sin perish as I look upon you.
And whatever sale of curd, milk, and clarified butter was made by me— / may that sin perish as I look upon you.
And having given hope to others, that it was rendered fruitless by me— / may that sin perish as I look upon you.
Twice-born people and beggars were looked upon by me with an angry glance— / may that sin perish as I look upon you.
Givers of a means of livelihood were reviled by me in anger— / may that sin perish as I look upon you.
What need of saying much here? Sins accumulated over many births / have gone to destruction as I look upon you.
I have attained my purpose, I have attained my purpose, I have attained my purpose, without doubt! / Homage to you, homage to you, homage to you, O Lord of the world!
Having spoken thus, that twice-born, his body bristling with horripilation out of devotion, / fell down, O Jaimini, at the two lovely lotus feet of Viṣṇu.

The Blessed Lord said:
“Rise up, rise up, O twice-born! I am pleased with your devotion.
Tell me what you desire; that I will surely grant to you.”

Bhadratanu said:
“O Supreme Lord, O Govinda, O compassionate one, O Supreme Acyuta!
Who in the world can obtain that which has just now been attained by me?

Nevertheless, I ask one boon in your presence, O Murāri:
in birth after birth, let my devotion to you remain firm, O Lord!

Whoever is a person that recites with devotion this hymn composed by me,
