may you, being well-pleased, grant all of their desired wishes.”

The Blessed Lord said:
“This boon has been granted to you, O twice-born; there is no doubt about this.
Moreover, O wise one, friendship with you is desired by me.

You are not fit to be my servant; here you and I are equals, O twice-born.
Therefore, friendship with you has now been formed by me.”

Vyāsa said:
Then Lord Nārāyaṇa, compassionate and affectionate to his devotees,
formed a friendship with that virtuous soul, O Jaimini.

Hari joyfully gave him the garland that hung upon his own neck;
and that twice-born too gave a garland of tulasī to Hari with devotion.

Stretching out his four arms, Hari embraced him;
and that twice-born master too joyfully embraced Viṣṇu.

Having thus established friendship with that brāhmaṇa,
Hari, compassionate and receptive to devotion, vanished right there.

From then on, day after day, in that sacred place of Puruṣottama,
Hari engaged in playing with a ball together with that brāhmaṇa.
Once, seeing that brāhmaṇa weakened, Hari, full of compassion, / spoke words out of affection for a friend, O sage among brāhmaṇas:
The Lord said: / "Friend, why are you weak? By whom has your wealth been taken away? / What anxiety is in your heart, friend? You ought to tell that."
Bhadratanu said: / "For your pleasure, O Lord of the world, austerity is ever performed by me in this way. / Because of that, my body undergoes weakness, O Lord."
The Lord said: / "Just as I am pleased with you, friend, I am not so pleased with anyone else. / Why then do you perform mortification of the body, O best of the twice-born?
Seeing you weak, distress arises in my heart. / Therefore abandon all mortification of the body, O best of the twice-born."

With his own upper garment, his own clothes and ornaments, with two beautiful golden buds, / and with the radiant bracelets of his own hands, that brāhmaṇa was adorned by the Lord of the gods himself.
Taking the crown from his own forehead, and a pair of anklets from his feet, / and the gold necklace from the region of his own neck, Kṛṣṇa, the Lord, gave [them] to that foremost of brāhmaṇas.
Adorned with those ornaments bestowed by the holy Hari, this meritorious twice-born man, / skilled in the game of ball, would play constantly with Kṛṣṇa, who was handsome as a dark lotus.
Once Dānta saw him there, his limbs adorned with ornaments, the pair of his lips charming with the red tint of betel, / wearing divine garments and an exquisite upper cloth, his face smiling.
Dānta said: / "Good Bhadratanu, even now you do not abandon your sinful disposition, / though your conduct has been seen to be censured by all people!
Since you were made my disciple, everything indeed is [now] an ornament [to you]. / And yet, the arrogant, the ill-behaved, the pitiless, the intent on sin,
and the destroyer of the guru's fame—these five are defilers of discipleship; / [as are] the non-devoted, the loquacious, and likewise the fickle-minded,
and one who censures the guru behind his back—these are declared the basest of disciples. / Knowing good character, a disciple should be accepted by the discerning.
Because knowledge residing in a wicked person brings sorrow even to gurus; / and what knowledge has been declared fame-giving by those who see reality,
those [teachings] residing in a wicked person immediately destroy the tree of the guru's fame. / Meritorious deeds are never pleasing to the sinful,
just as fragrant sandalwood is not pleasing to flies, / [and] just as donkeys are not satisfied by sweet food and drink,
so wicked people are not satisfied by the thought of dharma. / Fortune, out of fear of ill-repute, and dharma that grants all desires,
would never attach to a wicked person; or if it attaches, it goes to ruin. / The supreme knowledge which is obtained by good fortune in every birth—
even if one occasionally obtains it, destiny then intervenes."
Bhadratanu said: / "You speak the truth, O sage among brāhmaṇas; I am not versed in the scriptures. / Through me as your disciple, no ill-repute will ever arise for you.
By your favor, O best of the twice-born, all my desire / has reached fulfillment, since you alone are rare in the world."
Dānta said: / "What desire of yours, O brāhmaṇa, has reached fulfillment? Speak! / How was the completion of your austerities accomplished so quickly?"
Bhadratanu said: / "With slight effort indeed, the direct vision of Hari was attained by me, / by whose command, O guru, daily rites and the like were abandoned by me.
His own upper cloth and garment, and a pair of golden pitchers, / the bracelet from his own hand, and the crown from his own forehead,
the anklets from his own feet, and his own pearl necklace he gave; / so pleased with me was Lord Viṣṇu, O best of the twice-born.
Making friendship with me, the dispeller of his servant's sorrow remains; / I play a game of ball constantly with him, O guru.
Hearing this word of mine, although you may not believe [it], / nevertheless it was spoken by me with conviction in your presence."
Dānta said: / "Though Viṣṇu, the all-pervading Lord, was worshipped by me for seven thousand years with supreme devotion, / he did not grant me his direct vision.
Oh! Having worshipped Viṣṇu for only five days, O best of men, / the direct vision, difficult to attain even for the gods, was attained by you!
Blessed are you, fulfilled are you! You are truly called a visible god, / since the master lovingly formed a friendship with you.
If there is affection for me in you, O best of the twice-born, / tell me, O brāhmaṇa: How [can one attain] that rare direct vision of Viṣṇu?"
Vyāsa said: / Thus addressed by his guru, the wise brāhmaṇa, devoted to the worship of Viṣṇu, / went to his own hermitage in the forest, filled with wonder.
Then, having gone on another day and played the ball game, / he spoke thus to the compassionate Lord of the world, full of humility:
Bhadratanu said: / "My guru desires your direct vision, O Lord of the gods. / What is your command while he waits? Tell, O compassionate Lord, O husband of Kamalā!
That brāhmaṇa is exclusively devoted to you, O lotus-eyed one! / Therefore, O foremost of the gods, you ought to grant him your direct vision."
The Lord said: / "O foremost of brāhmaṇas, by you I was worshipped with supreme devotion through many births; / therefore my direct vision has now been given to you.
Having worshipped me for only a few days, that wise brāhmaṇa / desires to see me, who am unseen even by the gods.
Yet he too is my great devotee, intent on my worship; / therefore, at some time, that twice-born man will attain my direct vision."
Vyāsa said: / Hearing his words, that brāhmaṇa again spoke with devotion / to the husband of Kamalā, to Keśava, the destroyer of distress:
Bhadratanu said: / "If there is grace toward me, O Lord of gods, O Lord of the world, / then grant your direct vision before me, O lover of your devotees!
My guru begged for your direct vision as his teacher's fee, O Lord; / having granted the direct vision to my guru, protect me, O Lord!"
The Lord said: / "Since the teacher's fee of my direct vision was surely pledged by you, / then bring your guru here and cause him to have my direct vision."
Commanded thus by him, Bhadratanu then went with joy / to the excellent hermitage of his guru; his guru had returned.
When that brāhmaṇa Dānta, the best of givers, arrived, Hari / showed himself endowed with all auspicious marks.
Then, beholding Hari, that brāhmaṇa who practiced devotion to Hari, / joining his palms in reverence, praised him, his eyes filled with tears of joy.
Dānta said: / "O compassionate one, O beloved of Kamalā, O protector of those who have taken refuge! / Reverence to you, reverence to you, reverence to you, reverence, reverence!
Today my birth is fruitful; today my austerity is fruitful; / today everything of mine is fruitful, [for] your direct vision has been attained by me!
Whatever words I considered beforehand, O Lord, O Lord of Śrī, / have poured forth before you, who are deep as ten million oceans.

There is no such hymn in the world, [even of] the Lord of speech, the Lord of the universe, / by which hymn I may produce pleasure in your mind.

"Protect, protect, O Lord, protect me! Be pleased, O Lord of the world! / Choose me, even if only as a servant of the servants of the servants of your servants."
Vyāsa said: / Then, smiling, the Lord of gods, who accepts devotion, full of compassion, / placing his lotus hand upon his head, spoke thus, O Jaimini:
The Lord said: / "You are my devotee, O best of the twice-born; my direct vision has been attained by you. / By my grace, everything will indeed be auspicious for you."
Vyāsa said: / Having embraced that Dānta and that Bhadratanu with love, the Supreme Lord immediately vanished right there, O brahmin.
In that excellent and sacred field of Puruṣottama, which is difficult to attain, / having seen Hari through practical yogas, Dānta went to the supreme abode.
That brahmin Bhadratanu too, devoted to devotion to Hari, / at the end of his lifespan attained liberation, which is difficult even for the gods to attain.
If one worships the Supreme Lord with devotion even for a single day, / the sin committed across many births [is destroyed, and] love for Hari increases.
Even today, all thirty gods, even Brahmā and the others, O Jaimini, / do not fully know the power of a devotee of Hari on earth.
This land of ritual action, O brahmin, is difficult to attain even from heaven, / where, having worshipped Viṣṇu, mortals become praised by the gods.
All the thirty gods, Indra and the others, terrified of the exhaustion of their good merits, / constantly converse among themselves, O best of brahmins:
“When will we again go to the land of ritual action? / When will we perform the worship of the husband of Śrī Kamalā there?
Extremely fortunate are these people, greater even than us, / who worship Lord Hari in the difficult-to-attain realm of Bhārata!
Ah, who is capable of describing the virtues of the realm of Bhārata, / where, having worshipped Hari previously, we attained godhood?”
Thus all the hosts of gods, Indra and the others, O best of brahmins, / constantly praise that region of the land of Bhārata which bestows auspiciousness.
Having obtained birth there, one by whom Hari is not worshipped / has no equal seen or heard of anywhere in the world of transmigration.
Truly, truly, again it is stated, truly indeed: / the mortals who worship the Self of the universe even once,
or untiringly, O brahmin, with firm devotion in the land of ritual action, / freed from sins committed by their own hands, go swiftly to absolute solitude.

7.18.m: Jaimini said: / That which was declared by you as the foremost sacred place, Puruṣottama— / tell me its glorification, O teacher, if you have favor toward me.
Vyāsa said: / Listen in brief, O brahmin, to the glorification of Puruṣottama; / who in this world is capable of declaring it fully without Viṣṇu?
On the shore of the salt ocean is the city named Puruṣottama; / that city, O best of brahmins, is difficult to attain even from heaven.
Since glorious Puruṣottama resides in that city Himself, / it is therefore called Puruṣottama by the knowers of names.
That field is difficult to attain, O brahmin; measuring ten yojanas all around, / embodied beings staying there are seen by the gods as four-armed.
Entering that field, all indeed become forms of Viṣṇu; / therefore, no discrimination should be made there by the wise.
Even if touched by an outcaste, food is to be taken there by the twice-born, / because there an outcaste is manifestly Viṣṇu, O best of brahmins.
There Lakṣmī is the cook of the food, and Janārdana Himself is the eater; / therefore cooked rice there, O brahmin, is difficult to attain even for deities.
That which is the leftover of Hari’s meal, sacred, difficult to obtain on earth— / the people who eat that food, their liberation is not hard to attain.
All the thirty gods, Brahmā and the others, coming daily, eat / that extremely rare food; what then to say of humans?
He whose mind does not delight in that extremely rare food— / all the great sages declare him to be an enemy of Viṣṇu.
Just as the water of the Gaṅgā is everywhere sacred on earth, O brahmin, / so that sin-destroying food is sacred everywhere.
Even though that divine food is soft, O best of brahmins, / it is nevertheless like the belly of a saw in rending sins.
His previously accumulated sins will surely reach destruction, / whose devotion arises toward that extremely rare food.
The merit accumulated across many births will perish for him / in whose mind devotion does not arise toward that food, O best of brahmins.
In the lake of Indradyumna, and likewise in the pool of Mārkaṇḍeya, / and in the Rohiṇī [pool], and in the ocean, and in the waters of the Śvetagaṅgā,
those mortals who bathe endowed with a devotional disposition, / for them there is no rebirth on this surface of the earth.
The ancestors gratified with the waters of the salt ocean, O brahmin, / freed from all suffering, go to the abode of Hari.
This ocean is proclaimed by the seers of truth as the king of sacred bathing places; / therefore, every action performed there becomes inexhaustible.
The worship of ancestors, as well as charity, the worship of the Lord’s feet, / recitation, sacrifice, and other acts in that delightful field—
whatever action a mortal performs for the purpose of pleasing Viṣṇu, / all of that becomes inexhaustible; there is no doubt about this.
Those mortals who behold Balabhadra, Subhadrā, / and lotus-eyed Kṛṣṇa, for them nothing is difficult to attain.
Without seeing glorious Jagannātha, Subhadrā, and Bala, / a mortal does not attain liberation, even though performing hundreds of meritorious deeds.

One whose body is made red there by a blow of the cane, / to him all the gods, Indra and the others, bow down, O best of brahmins.

Standing in the sky, Śakra and all the hosts of gods, O twice-born, / moving in their aerial chariots, spoke to one another, filled with joy:
“When will the husband of Kamalā grant human birth to us? / Only as humans will we then go to see Lord Hari.
When will our bodies also become red / by a blow of the cane in the field of glorious Puruṣottama?”
All the gods, Indra and the others, in that boon-granting field, / always long for blows of the cane, O best of brahmins.
Those mortals who behold the Imperishable Banyan Tree there with devotion, / freed from sins accumulated in millions of births, go to the supreme state.
Subhadrā, Balabhadra, and faultless Jagannātha, / Śvetamādhava, Lord of gods, and the pool of Mārkaṇḍeya,
Jyāmeśvara, Hanūmat, and the Imperishable Banyan Tree there, O brahmin— / those mortals who behold them with devotion have eternal liberation.
Those mortals who with devotion behold Govinda swinging on a swing / in the month of Phālguna during those three [days], listen to their merit:
Freed from all sins, in the end they go to Hari’s abode; / having obtained knowledge right there, they attain liberation, which is exceedingly rare.
He who sees Jagannātha in the month of Caitra during the Vāruṇī festival, / upon dying enters the body of Jagannātha, O Jaimini.
And he who sees the Lord of the world in the month of Vaiśākha on the bright eleventh / and on the third [lunar day], that man is liberated indeed.
The mortal who enters the great bath of the Lord of the world, / for him, O brahmin-seer, all wishes are fulfilled.
All the thirty gods, Brahmā and the others, standing in the sky, / behold the great bath of the Lord of the world, endowed with a devotional disposition.
And having seen faultless Jagannātha on the great full moon of Jyeṣṭha, O brahmin-seer, / a mortal attains that supreme abode of Viṣṇu.

Whoever sees the Lord of Kamalā and Balabhadra
going to the Guṇḍikā pavilion in the month of Āṣāḍha is liberated; there is no doubt about this.

Whoever sees the lotus-eyed Jagannātha mounted upon his chariot
has no rebirth in this world, which brings all suffering.

And when people view Subhadrā mounted on her chariot with devotion,
the Blessed Lord cuts through their suffering-causing bond of worldly existence.

A woman who is childless or whose children have died, who beholds Subhadrā,
becomes one with many offspring, with living children, O twice-born.

An unfortunate woman or a woman barren after one child who beholds Subhadrā
shall certainly become a woman beloved of her husband and having many offspring.

And the man who sees Kṛṣṇa, Balabhadra, and Subhadrā
stationed in the Guṇḍikā pavilion attains the supreme state.

And whoever is sick or distressed and sees Hari in the Guṇḍikā pavilion
is at once freed from disease and grief, O Jaimini.

Indeed, one who is childless and sees Jagannātha stationed in the Guṇḍikā pavilion,
O best of the twice-born, obtains a Vaiṣṇava son.

One seeking learning obtains learning; one seeking wealth obtains wealth;
one seeking a wife obtains a wife; one seeking liberation attains liberation.

A king who has fallen from his kingdom, who sees Hari with devotion
in the Guṇḍikā pavilion, O twice-born, recovers his own kingdom.

One who is beset by enemies, who beholds Hari with devotion
in the Guṇḍikā pavilion, O twice-born seer, his enemies are destroyed.

Whoever is severely oppressed by a king and sees him in the Guṇḍikā pavilion
would immediately bring that king under his own control.

The Guṇḍikā festival is considered the foremost of all pilgrimages;
therefore it should be undertaken by humans, even leaving aside hundreds of duties.

And the mortal who sees Hari in that delightful sacred place
at his reclining and his rising is honored even by the gods.

Who on earth is able to speak the glorification of Puruṣottama,
by mere entry into which a mortal becomes Nārāyaṇa?

What is the need of much speaking here? It is stated in brief by me:
Puruṣottama is the greatest of all sacred places.

Wishing to cross over this extremely deep ocean of worldly existence, which bestows misery and is a resort for a multitude of perilous sins,
one should behold this best of deities, Puruṣottama, in the sacred place named Puruṣottama, which bestows all happiness.
